title: Bitcoin ETF inflows fade as price pressure tests ETF buyers’ $81,300 cost basis
summary: Bitcoin ETF demand returned last week, then faded. Now price is testing the ETF buyers’ cost basis Money came back into US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds last week, but it didn’t stay. The funds took in about $1.07 billion over the first three sessions, then lost $773.5 million over the final two, according to preliminary Farside data. That left a provisional net inflow of $301.2 million for the week to October 23. Bitcoin, meanwhile, slipped back toward $80,000, close to the level where the average ETF buyer would start losing money. --- Earlier: Bitcoin buyers are fighting back, but sellers aren't finished. Here are the two prices swing traders should watch Strategy bitcoin purchases shrink as buybacks take priority ahead of earnings --- What happened The week opened strongly. Spot bitcoin ETFs took in $526.7 million on Monday, $23.2 million on Tuesday and $524.8 million on Wednesday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led the way, drawing $665.2 million on Monday, its largest single-day inflow since October 2025. The mood then reversed. Thursday brought $635.6 million in outflows, the largest daily withdrawal since June, followed by another $137.9 million on Friday. IBIT itself saw $254.1 million leave on Thursday and $110.3 million on Friday, though it still finished the week with net inflows of $565.7 million. title: Brazil ETF tumbles nearly 15% in Tokyo after Lula’s comeback runoff win
summary: The Tokyo ETF move is an early and thin-volume signal, so the real test comes when Brazilian markets open, with the real, the local rates curve and the Bovespa likely to bear the brunt of any repricing. Goldman Sachs’ figures describe an extreme scenario rather than a base case, but they frame the scale of the potential move, with the long end of the curve and the currency most exposed. Positioning matters: markets rallied after the first round on expectations of a different outcome, so some of the selling may reflect that trade being unwound rather than a fresh view on policy. Spillover to other Latin American currencies and EM risk sentiment is possible if the selloff is disorderly, while a contained reaction could see dip-buyers emerge quickly. --- Lula pulled off a rare second-round comeback, and the first verdict from markets, a near 15% drop in a Tokyo-listed Brazil ETF, suggests investors had been positioned for the other result.
